Combat layout: light/strong attack, jump and action in the diamond; Blade Mode (LB), Ninja Run (RB), lock-on (RT), sub-weapon (LT) and dodge (X+A) around it. Drag a free spot on the right side to move the camera; a quick tap centers it. In game, the gear (top left) opens these options with the game paused.

Zandatsu is the Android port of Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance (Xbox 360), statically recompiled with the ReXGlue SDK: the game code runs natively, only the GPU is emulated.

Thanks to: the ReXGlue SDK team, iExplosiveRage (Android SDK fork), the Xenia project (GPU emulation), SDL, libadrenotools (bylaws) and the Turnip/Mesa driver builders (Mr. Purple, StevenMXZ, K11MCH1).
Unofficial, non-commercial fan project. No game files are included: you need your own legal copy. Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance belongs to Konami and PlatinumGames.
Game paused while this menu is open.
Analog stick for walking (MGR is 3D); the 8-way D-pad is optional.
The game stops while the controls menu (gear in game) or the game menu (Back + Start) is open.
Resolution and the GPU safe mode apply the next time the game opens.
Automatic: they show up when you touch the screen and hide when you use a controller.
The game writes much more to the log. Use it to report a problem; it can cost a little performance.
Switch controls: combat / menus / full pad
Every 5 s the log records FPS, GPU time per frame and the GPU clock and load. Light; use it to report stutter.
Copies the full-screen effects straight to the texture, skipping two conversions. Less GPU load.
Also skips copying the effects into the game memory (only the texture is filled). Faster; turn it off if some effect looks wrong.
For graphical glitches with Turnip on Adreno 6xx (e.g. 650). Applied when the game reopens; combine freely. The system driver ignores the TU_DEBUG ones.
No dynamic rendering and stencil export
Game memory in one block (512 MB)
Each pass draws into its own image with no copies between them (less GPU work). Turn off if parts of the image go missing.
Each shader is compiled for the format of its textures, without the extra per-pixel branches and sampling (much faster texturing). Turn off if colors or textures look wrong.
What the game is drawn at, then scaled to the screen. 720p is the console resolution; 360p/540p draw fewer pixels (faster), 2K = 1440p (2x), 4K = 2160p (3x).
2K and 4K need much more GPU memory. On Mali GPUs keep 720p or lower.
Each category on its own, like PC games. The profiles above change these same options.
Leave them on unless something looks wrong.
Different version: this port needs the default.xex it was recompiled from
different version (not the one the port uses)
The media folder was not found next to default.xex (%1$s).
This is not the version of Metal Gear Rising the port was recompiled from (%1$s).
This file is not an Xbox 360 disc image (%1$s). Use a full .iso (XGD2), not a GOD/XEX package.
Clears the game\'s buffers at 1x and scales them (less GPU work at 2x/3x). Turn off if the edges of the image flicker.
MGR runs at 60 FPS. The 30 FPS hack keeps the game at full speed and only draws every other frame: half the GPU work, for weaker GPUs (Mali).

Snapdragon 865 or newer (e.g. Retroid Pocket 5) should run the game with the system driver; Turnip is optional, in the Drivers tab.

Mali GPUs (e.g. Mali-G57 in the RG Cube) run it slower: use the Light preset (540p, 30 FPS hack) in the Performance tab.

If the game closes or looks wrong, the app shows what happened and how to send the log on Discord.
News, help and builds of the port
Tools to find problems. Leave them as they are unless a report asks you to change something.
What to send when reporting a problem
In the game, open the menu (Back or the pause button) → Debug → Capture frames. The next frames are saved and go into Export logs.

The game runs at 60 and a generated frame is shown between each two real ones (motion estimation on the GPU, about 1-3 ms per frame). Adds one frame of latency (about 8 ms). Fast moves can show small artifacts.
120 FPS needs a 120 Hz screen; this one goes up to %1$d Hz.
This configuration asks for 120 FPS, but this screen can\'t show it: the game will present at 60 Hz. Pick 30 or 60.
Sets resolution, frame rate and filters at once, by how heavy they are for the GPU. The renderer optimizations stay on.
No 1080p: the renderer only multiplies 720p by whole numbers (1080p would be 1.5x). On a 1080p screen, 720p is scaled up and 2K is scaled down (sharper, much heavier).
Below 720p: less sharp, but the GPU draws only %1$d%% of the pixels. AMD FSR 1 helps the sharpness.
Above 720p the GPU draws %1$dx the pixels: only for the strongest GPUs.
360p, 30 FPS, FSR, no shadows or glow
540p, 30 FPS, FSR, no shadows or glow
540p, 60 FPS, FSR, no shadows or glow

Freezes the picture (the game stops, the GPU keeps redrawing the same frame) and turns the renderer shortcuts off one at a time, comparing pictures: shows which one breaks the image and how much each is worth. Unfreezes at the end. Result in Export logs.
Puts all logs, the self-test result and the latest capture in a zip in Download/.
Turnip is stable on this GPU. Builds people use: %1$s.

With Turnip active, TU_DEBUG=%1$s is applied automatically on this GPU.

Shader compiler: no UBO optimization (IR3 nouboopt)
Turnip bisect: change one driver option per game start
Next game start: step %1$s (of %2$d). Play a bit + render self-test at each start and send every zip.
30 FPS hack: same game speed, half the frames drawn.
Render self-test: in the game, open the menu → Debug → Render self-test. It freezes the picture by itself, turns the GPU shortcuts off one by one and compares pictures.
MGR controls on the touch screen
The fewest buttons, combos already joined

Left stick: walk · drag on the right: camera (tap = center, R3)
X light attack (+ stick toward the enemy = parry) · Y strong attack · A jump · B action / Zandatsu grab
LB hold: Blade Mode (cut with the camera drag or X/Y) · RB hold: Ninja Run · RT lock-on · LT sub-weapon
Dodge button = X+A (with a direction) · small cross: ↑ Augment, ← → weapons/items, ↓ use item · L3+R3: Ripper Mode
Start pause · Back Codec
Touch controls are off. The gear and pause buttons stay on the screen, and the Back button always opens this menu: turn them on again here.
Self-test finished: exporting the logs to Download/…
Self-test finished (export failed: use Export logs)
Effect passes are drawn straight into the texture the game reads, without the copy. Less GPU load; turn off if an effect looks wrong.
Skips repeated copies, empty draws and color loads that are overwritten anyway. Turn off if something flickers.
All renderer optimizations off: the plain emulated path. Slower; use it to check if a glitch comes from an optimization.
Safe mode is on: the switches below are ignored.
Everything the app and the game record, for bug reports
Need help? Save the log, join our Discord and post the zip in the logs channel, with your device and what you were doing.
The game stopped by itself while playing. Try a lighter preset in Performance, or the system driver in Drivers. If it keeps happening, send the log.
The game closed before showing the first frame. Check the game files on Home (Verify files) and try again. If it keeps happening, send the log.
Turnip failed to start the game

The game closed before showing anything 3 times in a row with the Turnip driver. Try the system driver (button below) or another Turnip version in Drivers. This port is optimized for Turnip, so please send the log too: it helps us fix it.
The driver could not be downloaded or installed. Check the connection, or that the file is an AdrenoTools .zip (with meta.json and the .so).
The .iso or the game files are damaged, incomplete or not the expected version. Make a new dump of your disc (full XGD2 .iso) and import it again.
The game could not be copied. Check the free space and that the file or folder is still available, then try again.
The game opens and closes by itself, one driver option per start (~40 s each). Do not touch the device; at the end the log zip is saved to Download.
Off saves ~2.6 ms per frame on the RG Cube with no visible change in the tested scenes.
Half-precision math in the game shaders: faster on Mali and Adreno; may show banding or wrong effects. Applies on the next start.
Runs the game 8x faster during the company logos at startup, until the title screen.
Shadows cast on the screen. Off saves ~3 ms per frame on the RP5; the image stays normal, only without these shadows.
High: shadows cast on the scene (~3 ms on the RP5). Off: normal image, just without those shadows. Medium comes with the native shadow renderer.
High: glow with blur (~3 ms). Medium: glow without blur.
Low (experimental): without the strike particles (sparks, dust). Hair and clothes stay. Report anything that disappears and should not.
Native: the game\'s Direct3D on Vulkan (Renut), faster and sharper. Emulated: the Xbox 360 GPU (Xenia), with FSR, FXAA and 30/120 FPS.
No profile chosen: pick one, or set the options below yourself.
The game runs at 60 FPS (its own rate). The 30 FPS hack and 120 FPS are emulated renderer options.
720p is the console\'s. 540p draws 56% of the pixels; 1080p, 1440p and 4K draw 2.25x, 4x and 9x and are scaled down to the screen.
The sun\'s shadows (shadow map and screen shadow pass). Off: the scene is lit everywhere.
The glow around lights and the sword. Off: the original image, without glow.
